author: Mark Atwood
text: Rust idiom confidence: ~30% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: none filed (every finding was checked at the cited site and the rewrite alternative was named). Uncertainty driven by: (1) I read all handler-level src files but only sampled backend.rs (789 lines) and skipped memory.rs entirely (3121 lines) — the reference MemoryBackend is gated behind feature='memory' and the AGENTS.md banner explicitly says it's not production, so idiom misses there are lower-stakes, but a serious Rust shop would flag clone() patterns / unwrap-on-Result-of-Mutex / await-holding-lock in the in-memory layer if any exist; (2) integration tests (~4708 lines integration.rs alone) were not sampled — any idiom misses there are tooling/test concerns not API concerns, but a senior Rust reviewer might still flag e.g. test-helper duplication, .unwrap()s that should be .expect() with diagnostic text, etc.; (3) the canonical-template propagation rule means several of my findings (.29, .31, .32) would replicate to ~7 sibling extension-server crates if propagated — I did not check whether the same patterns exist in jmap-mail-server (the canonical), which would change them from 'chat-server local issue' to 'workspace-wide convention issue' worth a single sweep bead rather than per-crate findings. Would raise confidence if: (a) memory.rs was sampled for clippy::await_holding_lock / unwrap on lock results / unnecessary .clone() on Arc<...>, (b) jmap-mail-server was diffed against chat-server for the same string-dispatch / positional-constructor patterns, (c) cargo clippy --workspace -- -W clippy::pedantic was run against this diff to surface lints I'd miss by eyeball.
